issues.legal_issue: A joint mortgagor who is liable for the entire joint mortgage debt must count that entire liability when determining eligibility for agricultural debt relief, unless the governing statute provides for apportionment.
material_facts: The applicants jointly executed a usufructuary mortgage, and each mortgagor was liable under its terms for the entire debt.

When the entire joint debt was counted for each applicant, each applicant’s total debts exceeded the statutory eligibility ceiling; dividing the mortgage debt into equal shares would have brought each below it.
The statute’s definitions and provisions governing joint liability and debt adjustment did not provide a basis for splitting this joint mortgage debt.
issues.conclusion: Each applicant was liable for the entire mortgage debt and was therefore not a debtor eligible for relief under the Act; the High Court’s contrary decision was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under the ordinary rule reflected in the Transfer of Property Act, each debtor jointly liable for a debt is liable for the whole debt. The Saurashtra Agricultural Debtors’ Relief Act, including sections 2(5), 2(6)(i), 7, 16, 19, 20, 21 and 29, did not alter that rule for the joint mortgage debt at issue. The Court approved Ambu Rama Mhatro v. Bhau Halya Patel, AIR 1957 Bom. 6, and Dave Sadashiv Jayakrishna v. Rana Govubha, (1962) 3 Guj. L.R. 1007, and distinguished V. Ramaswami Ayyangar v. T.N.V. Kailasa Thavar, [1951] S.C.R. 292, which involved a different statutory provision and an executing court’s limits.

rule.if: agricultural_debt_relief_application and joint_mortgage_liability and each_coborrower_liable_for_entire_debt and no_statutory_apportionment_rule and individual_total_debt_exceeds_eligibility_limit

predicates.agricultural_debt_relief_application: The applicants sought adjustment or scaling down of their debts under an agricultural debt-relief scheme.
predicates.joint_mortgage_liability: The applicants incurred a mortgage debt jointly.
predicates.each_coborrower_liable_for_entire_debt: The mortgage terms made each co-borrower liable for the entire debt.
predicates.no_statutory_apportionment_rule: The applicable scheme contained no provision that apportioned this joint mortgage debt among the co-borrowers.
predicates.individual_total_debt_exceeds_eligibilit: Each applicant’s total debt, counting the entire joint mortgage debt, exceeded the scheme’s eligibility ceiling.

issues.definition: When applicants seek agricultural debt relief for a joint mortgage debt, each is liable for the whole debt if the agreement so provides and the scheme does not apportion it, and applicants whose individual total debts exceed the eligibility limit are ineligible for relief.

issues.legal_issue: A Single Judge of a High Court is ordinarily bound by judgments of coordinate courts and by judgments of Division Benches and Full Benches of that High Court.
material_facts: A Single Judge of the High Court had expressed conclusions about whether a Single Judge was bound by earlier decisions of that High Court.
The Supreme Court had already addressed and rejected similar conclusions in an earlier case.
issues.conclusion: A Single Judge is ordinarily bound to accept as correct judgments of courts of coordinate jurisdiction and of Division Benches and Full Benches of the same High Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court reaffirmed Tribhovandas Purshottamdas Thakkar v. Ratilal Motilal Patel, AIR 1968 S.C. 372, which states that a Single Judge of a High Court is ordinarily bound by judgments of courts of coordinate jurisdiction and by judgments of Division Benches and Full Benches of that Court.

predicates.single_judge_high_court_case: A legal issue is being decided by a Single Judge of a High Court.
predicates.prior_coordinate_or_larger_bench_judgmen: A coordinate court, Division Bench, or Full Bench of the same High Court has already decided the point.

issues.definition: When a Single Judge decides a point already decided by a coordinate court or a larger bench of the same High Court, the Single Judge is ordinarily bound by that earlier judgment.
